findings.why: The double-dash structure enclosing the long bag description made me lose the main clause — 'she came in past the kitchen and put her bag on the chair' — and I had to reconnect to 'and came into him and put her arms around him' after the aside.
The dangling 'for' at the end of 'the thing she had built her whole adult life around being looked at for' forced me to re-read to connect it back to the blue eyes.
'A thing she said with a knife in it' — I couldn't determine what 'it' referred to or what the knife metaphor meant. A diet described cuttingly? A diet that was itself sharp? I never resolved it.
'Finding it had stopped being the thing she was doing' — the self-referential structure and unclear 'it' made me re-read to work out what had stopped being what.
'The point did not survive the next pass' — the metaphor required a beat to decode: her attempt to prove she was still eating didn't survive his hands moving near her breasts.
'They had spent the evening inside' — 'they' is grammatically ambiguous between the breasts and the bra, and 'made nothing of' is an unfamiliar usage, so I re-read to sort out the reference.
'The word for what he held stayed behind his face, and he let his hands say the nearer things' — the abstraction required a moment to decode: he didn't say the word, he touched instead.
'Landing somewhere he didn't govern' — I couldn't tell where her sounds were landing (in him? in her?) and the metaphor stayed opaque.
'The wanted position' — the play on words (sexual position vs. the social position of being desired) took a beat to catch.
The em-dash interruption 'she could not — she could feel that she could not — get them back' broke the syntactic flow and I had to re-read to reconstruct the sentence's logic.

'Under it, inseparable from it' — I couldn't determine what 'it' referred to (the disjunction? the feeling from the previous sentence?), and the later 'it had not come from her' compounded the reference problem.
'Nothing happened to her' — the apparent contradiction with everything just described required a gear-shift to understand she's describing her old defensive state, not the current reality.
Very long sentence contrasting her performed smile with his genuine one; the length required attention to hold both sides of the contrast through to the end.
